Construct the skeleton category by taking the quotient of objects. This construction gives a
preorder with nice definitional properties, but is only really appropriate for thin categories.
If your original category is not thin, you probably want to be using `skeleton` instead of this.

```lean
inferInstance.{u} {α : Sort u} [i : α] : α
```
***
`inferInstance` synthesizes a value of any target type by typeclass
inference. This function has the same type signature as the identity
function, but the square brackets on the `[i : α]` argument means that it will
attempt to construct this argument by typeclass inference. (This will fail if
`α` is not a `class`.) Example:
```
#check (inferInstance : Inhabited Nat) -- Inhabited Nat

def foo : Inhabited (Nat × Nat) :=
  inferInstance

example : foo.default = (default, default) :=
  rfl
```

```lean
rfl.{u} {α : Sort u} {a : α} : a = a
```
***
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

***
Starting with `A : MonoOver X`, we can take its equivalence class in `Subobject X`

***
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

```
def foo : Inhabited (Nat × Nat) :=
```

```lean
rfl.{u} {α : Sort u} {a : α} : a = a
```
***
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

***
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

```lean
  (P : Subobject X) : (mapIsoToOrderIso e) P = (map e.hom).obj P
```

```lean

  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {Y : D} (F : MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y) : Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y
```
***
Any functor `MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y` descends to a functor
`Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y`, because `MonoOver Y` is thin.

```lean
CategoryTheory.MonoOver.exists.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasImages C] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y
```
***
In the case where `f` is not a monomorphism but `C` has images,
we can still take the "forward map" under it, which agrees with `MonoOver.map f`.

***
*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subobject.MonoOver*

```lean
CategoryTheory.Subobject.exists.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasImages C] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y
```
***
The functor from subobjects of `X` to subobjects of `Y` given by
sending the subobject `S` to its "image" under `f`, usually denoted $\exists_f$.
For instance, when `C` is the category of types,
viewing `Subobject X` as `Set X` this is just `Set.image f`.

This functor is left adjoint to the `pullback f` functor (shown in `existsPullbackAdj`)
provided both are defined, and generalises the `map f` functor, again provided it is defined.

***
`HasPullbacks` represents a choice of pullback for every pair of morphisms

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001W>

***
*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.HasPullback*

```lean
CategoryTheory.Subobject.exists.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasImages C] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y
```
***
The functor from subobjects of `X` to subobjects of `Y` given by
sending the subobject `S` to its "image" under `f`, usually denoted $\exists_f$.
For instance, when `C` is the category of types,
viewing `Subobject X` as `Set X` this is just `Set.image f`.

This functor is left adjoint to the `pullback f` functor (shown in `existsPullbackAdj`)
provided both are defined, and generalises the `map f` functor, again provided it is defined.

```lean
CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasPullbacks C] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject X
```
***
When `C` has pullbacks, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` induces a functor `Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject X`,
by pulling back a monomorphism along `f`.

```lean
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerAdjunction.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {A : C} {B : D} {L : MonoOver A ⥤ MonoOver B} {R : MonoOver B ⥤ MonoOver A} (h : L ⊣ R) :
  lower L ⊣ lower R
```
***
An adjunction between `MonoOver A` and `MonoOver B` gives an adjunction
between `Subobject A` and `Subobject B`.

```lean
CategoryTheory.MonoOver.existsPullbackAdj.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasImages C]
  (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasPullbacks C] : MonoOver.exists f ⊣ MonoOver.pullback f
```
***
`exists` is adjoint to `pullback` when images exist 
***
*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subobject.MonoOver*

```lean
CategoryTheory.Subobject.existsPullbackAdj.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasImages C]
  (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasPullbacks C] : exists f ⊣ pullback f
```
***
`exists f : Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y` is
left adjoint to `pullback f : Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject X`.
